questions.statement: 1. What is the primary architectural difference between BSON and JSON in MongoDB?
options: BSON only supports plain string keys and values
BSON is a binary-encoded serialization format providing additional data types like Date and ObjectId
BSON requires a predefined relational schema
JSON compresses nested arrays faster than BSON

questions.statement: 2. What is the maximum single document size limit in MongoDB by default?
options: 4 MB
8 MB
16 MB
32 MB

questions.statement: 3. In MongoDB's ObjectId (12 bytes), which component makes up the first 4 bytes?
options: A 4-byte incrementing counter
A 4-byte random value unique to the machine
A 4-byte Unix epoch timestamp
A 4-byte process identifier

questions.statement: 4. Under the CAP theorem, how is a standard MongoDB replica set classified by default?
options: AP (Available and Partition-Tolerant)
CP (Consistent and Partition-Tolerant)
CA (Consistent and Available without network partitions)
None of the above

questions.statement: 5. What does the WiredTiger storage engine provide for write concurrency?
options: Global database locking
Collection-level locking
Document-level concurrency control
Field-level serialization

questions.statement: 6. What happens if a MongoDB query executes an aggregation pipeline with $sort without an index and exceeds 100 MB of RAM?
options: The query automatically switches to a full-table scan
It throws an error unless allowDiskUse: true is specified
The server terminates the connection and restarts WiredTiger
MongoDB truncates the sorted data

questions.statement: 7. Which write concern guarantees that an operation has been written to the majority of replica set nodes and committed to disk journals?
options: { w: 1, j: false }
{ w: "majority", j: true }
{ w: 2, j: false }

questions.statement: 8. What is a "Covered Query" in MongoDB?
options: A query wrapped in an ACID transaction
A query where all fields requested exist entirely within an index, avoiding document fetches
A query that utilizes sharding key partitions
A query run against secondary replica members only

questions.statement: 9. What is the fundamental restriction on Compound Indexes in MongoDB regarding Multi-key indexes?
options: No compound index can contain arrays
A compound index cannot include more than one field that contains an array
Array fields must always be at the end of the compound index
An index cannot hold both strings and arrays

questions.statement: 10. What does a Capped Collection in MongoDB provide?
options: Collections with strict document size schemas
High-throughput, fixed-size circular buffers that preserve insertion order
Encrypted storage collections
Collections with automated TTL indexing

questions.statement: 11. In Mongoose, what is the key conceptual difference between lean() queries and regular queries?
options: lean() executes directly on secondary nodes
lean() returns plain JavaScript objects, skipping Mongoose document hydration and change-tracking
lean() forces MongoDB to ignore schema validations during insert
lean() executes queries without requiring a database connection

questions.statement: 12. Do Mongoose validation rules run by default on findOneAndUpdate() operations?
options: Yes, all validators run unconditionally
No, update validators must be explicitly enabled via { runValidators: true }
Yes, but only for sub-documents
No, Mongoose never supports validation for updates

questions.statement: 13. In Mongoose middleware (hooks), which hook type does NOT have access to the document via this?
options: Document middleware (e.g., pre('save'))
Query middleware (e.g., pre('find'))
Custom instance methods
Post-init hooks

questions.statement: 14. What does Mongoose’s populate() method actually execute behind the scenes?
options: A database-level native SQL join
A client-side separate query to target collections using $in matching the IDs
A mandatory $lookup aggregation pipeline stage on every call
A secondary index join in WiredTiger

questions.statement: 15. What is the role of the __v field generated by Mongoose?
options: Tracking schema migration revisions
Serving as an internal version key for optimistic concurrency control on array modifications
Storing the MongoDB server version that wrote the document
Counting total read/write operations per document

questions.statement: 16. What is the purpose of Mongoose Virtuals?
options: Creating temporary collections on RAM disks
Defining document properties that can be manipulated but are not persisted to MongoDB
Running asynchronous background schema validations
Generating synthetic index trees

questions.statement: 17. In a MongoDB sharded cluster, which component routes client queries to the correct shards?
options: mongod primary node
mongos query router
Config server election coordinator
WiredTiger journal router

questions.statement: 18. What query condition leads to a "Scatter-Gather" query across a sharded cluster?
options: A query using a compound index
A query that does not include the shard key in its filter criteria
A query performing projecting suppression (_id: 0)
A query using aggregation without $match

questions.statement: 19. Which update operator appends a value to an array ONLY if the value does not already exist?
options: $push
$addToSet
$setUnion
$mergeArray

questions.statement: 20. What is the fundamental difference between $embed (embedding) and referencing in NoSQL schema design?
options: Referencing cannot enforce 1-to-many relationships
Embedding provides atomic single-document updates and fast reads; referencing avoids document-growth limits and duplicated data
Referencing requires all documents to reside in memory simultaneously
Embedding is strictly prohibited when arrays contain objects

questions.statement: 21. In MongoDB indexing, what is the ESL (Equality, Sort, Range) rule?
options: The order in which MongoDB sharding assigns keys
The best practice sequence for ordering fields in a compound index: Equality first, Sort second, Range last
The internal algorithm used to balance B-trees during split
The memory eviction priority for dirty cache pages

questions.statement: 22. What occurs when an un-indexed query execution outputs an IXSCAN stage followed by a COLLSCAN stage in an explain() output?
options: The index was used, but individual documents were fetched from disk to resolve fields (FETCH)
The query engine abandoned index scanning because of index fragmentation
The system is running a map-reduce batch fallback
The collection contains corrupted BSON trees

questions.statement: 23. In Mongoose, what is the key difference between Schema methods and statics?
options: methods run on schemas; statics run on fields
methods are instance methods on individual documents; statics are class methods on the compiled Model
methods cannot be asynchronous; statics can
statics run prior to validation; methods run after saving

questions.statement: 24. What does the MongoDB readConcern: "majority" guarantee?
options: The read query returns data calculated across all shards
The read returns data committed to and acknowledged by a majority of nodes, preventing dirty reads of rolled-back writes
The query reads only from primary cluster instances
Secondary nodes are bypassed completely

questions.statement: 25. What happens when you define a TTL (Time-to-Live) index on a compound index?
options: The document expires when the first timestamp is reached
TTL is not supported on compound indexes in MongoDB
The expiration interval is multiplied across indexed fields
It converts the index into a partial index

questions.statement: 26. What is the fundamental behavior of Mongoose's discriminators?
options: Providing field-level encryption based on user roles
A schema inheritance mechanism enabling multiple sub-schemas to share the same collection under an identifying key
Filtering documents during connection pool exhaustion
Forcing separate collection generation per inheritance tree

questions.statement: 27. Which operation in MongoDB is non-atomic?
options: Updating three fields on a single document via updateOne()
Modifying nested array elements inside one document
Updating multiple documents via standard updateMany() without multi-document transactions
Replacing an entire single document via replaceOne()

questions.statement: 28. In MongoDB Aggregation, what is the primary role of $facet?
options: Decrypting client-side collections
Executing multiple aggregation pipelines simultaneously within a single stage on the same input documents
Flattening multiple nested arrays into a single level
Enforcing uniqueness across fields

questions.statement: 29. Why might an aggregation pipeline stage using $lookup be inefficient if unindexed?
options: It forces the primary node to perform an election
It performs an unconditional full collection scan (COLLSCAN) on the from collection for every incoming document
It automatically invalidates the WiredTiger cache
It drops partial indexes across foreign keys

questions.statement: 30. What does the strict option do when set to true (default) in a Mongoose Schema?
options: It prevents saving documents if external HTTP calls are active
It ensures values not specified in the schema model are ignored and omitted from being saved to the database
It blocks queries containing unindexed parameters
It enforces JavaScript strict-mode evaluation on all hooks
